target.what: Total number of tokens processed (input plus output, including cached and reasoning tokens where reported) by all large language models worldwide during calendar year 2025, aggregated across both provider-operated consumer/enterprise products (chat apps, coding assistants, embedded features) and thi
target.publisher: None — no single official publisher; assembled from provider disclosures (Google, Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Alibaba, ByteDance, Baidu, xAI, Mistral, etc.), cloud/GPU-capacity estimates, and third-party trackers (OpenRouter, Poe, Artificial Analysis, Similarweb, a16z, Epoch AI)
target.cadence: Irregular; provider token disclosures are quarterly or ad hoc, third-party trackers are daily/monthly
target.caveats: Target period is completed relative to the 2026-10-22 cutoff, but full-year 2025 token totals are not reported by any single source. Definitions vary widely: input vs output vs cached vs reasoning tokens; tokens counted at API gateway vs model inference; consumer product usage often undisclosed. Wor

candidates.perspective: Major LLM providers (Google, Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Alibaba, ByteDance, Baidu, xAI) that periodically disclose token processing volumes
candidates.hypothesis: Sum of provider-reported token volumes (monthly/quarterly) across 2025 gives a lower bound on total tokens; scaling by estimated undisclosed share of each provider's traffic yields the total. Direction: reported totals understate true totals because consumer products and some API traffic are unreported.
candidates.data_to_find: All public token-volume disclosures for 2025: Google (monthly tokens processed, e.g. Gemini API and AI Overviews), Microsoft/Azure OpenAI token stats, OpenAI usage figures, Anthropic API token volumes, Meta AI usage, Alibaba Qwen token stats, ByteDance Doubao token stats, Baidu Ernie, xAI Grok. Need period, scope (API vs product), and whether input/output/cached included. Substitute: quarterly earnings call statements and developer blog posts.
search_hints: Google monthly tokens processed 2025 Gemini API

candidates.perspective: Cloud/GPU infrastructure operators and analysts estimating total inference compute
candidates.hypothesis: Total tokens ≈ (deployed inference GPU capacity in FLOP/s) × utilisation × seconds in 2025 ÷ average FLOP per token. Direction: capacity-based estimate constrains the upper bound and cross-checks provider disclosures. Transfer assumption: average FLOP/token depends on model size, batch size, and sparsity; must be estimated from model mix.
candidates.data_to_find: 2025 GPU/TPU/ASIC shipments and installed base allocated to inference (NVIDIA data-center revenue split, hyperscaler capex, Epoch AI or SemiAnalysis estimates), average utilisation rates, and average FLOP per token for the 2025 model mix (frontier vs small models). Substitute: total AI data-center power draw × tokens per joule benchmarks.
search_hints: AI data center power inference share 2025

candidates.perspective: Third-party API aggregators and model-routing platforms (OpenRouter, Poe, Artificial Analysis, Together, Fireworks)
candidates.hypothesis: Aggregator token volumes represent a measurable slice of API traffic; scaling by estimated aggregator share of total API tokens gives total API tokens. Direction: aggregator share is small but growing; useful for API-only sub-total and for model-mix weights.
candidates.data_to_find: OpenRouter monthly token volumes and model rankings for 2025, Poe/Quora usage stats, Artificial Analysis token throughput data, Together/Fireworks disclosed volumes. Need monthly series Jan–Dec 2025 and estimated share of total API market. Substitute: a16z or Menlo Ventures enterprise LLM API market reports with token or spend estimates.
search_hints: Menlo Ventures enterprise LLM API usage 2025

candidates.perspective: Consumer AI product usage trackers (Similarweb, Sensor Tower, a16z top-100 gen AI apps)
candidates.hypothesis: First-party product tokens ≈ (monthly active users) × (sessions per user) × (tokens per session). Direction: consumer product traffic is a large and growing share of total tokens; MAU × engagement × average tokens per interaction gives a bottom-up estimate. Transfer assumption: average tokens per session varies by product (chat vs coding vs search-augmented).
candidates.data_to_find: 2025 MAU and session/engagement data for ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Meta AI, Copilot, Doubao, Qwen, Grok, Perplexity; average tokens per query or session benchmarks. Substitute: app download and DAU estimates combined with published tokens-per-query figures.
search_hints: ChatGPT weekly active users 2025 tokens per query

candidates.perspective: Historical token-volume disclosures and growth trajectories from 2023–2024 to extrapolate 2025
candidates.hypothesis: Token volumes grew roughly exponentially 2023–2025; fitting a growth curve to earlier disclosed points (e.g. Google's 2024 monthly tokens, OpenAI 2023–2024 usage) and extrapolating to 2025 gives an independent estimate. Direction: growth rates of 5–10x per year imply 2025 totals far above 2024. Transfer assumption: growth rate stable through 2025.
candidates.data_to_find: Google monthly tokens processed 2024 (e.g. 9.7 trillion reported mid-2024), OpenAI tokens per day 2023–2024, Anthropic 2024 volumes, any 2023 baselines. Need consistent scope across years. Substitute: revenue growth of inference-heavy providers as a proxy.

candidates.perspective: Research firms and analysts publishing 2025 token-volume or inference-market forecasts (Epoch AI, Stanford AI Index, IDC, Gartner, a16z)
candidates.hypothesis: Published forecasts or estimates of 2025 total tokens or inference compute provide a direct anchor; comparing multiple forecasts bounds uncertainty. Direction: forecasts may be based on the same underlying disclosures, so treat as correlated. Transfer assumption: forecast scope matches target definition.
candidates.data_to_find: Epoch AI token-volume estimates, Stanford AI Index 2025/2026 token statistics, IDC/Gartner AI inference market forecasts with token or query volumes, a16z 'LLMflation' or token-consumption analyses. Need explicit 2025 full-year figures and methodology. Substitute: inference compute (FLOP) forecasts converted via FLOP/token.

candidates.perspective: Energy and data-center operators measuring inference electricity consumption
candidates.hypothesis: Total tokens ≈ (inference electricity consumption in 2025, kWh) ÷ (energy per token, kWh/token). Direction: bottom-up energy accounting constrains total tokens independent of provider disclosures. Transfer assumption: energy per token varies by model size and hardware; use model-mix-weighted average.
candidates.data_to_find: 2025 AI inference electricity consumption estimates (IEA, EPRI, LBNL, SemiAnalysis), data-center power split between training and inference, and measured energy-per-token benchmarks (e.g. kWh per 1000 tokens for GPT-4-class vs small models). Substitute: total data-center electricity × inference share.
search_hints: energy per token LLM inference benchmark
data center power training vs inference 2025

candidates.perspective: Model-mix and token-type composition analysts (input vs output, cached vs uncached, reasoning tokens)
candidates.hypothesis: Total tokens = API tokens + product tokens; each splits into input/output/cached/reasoning. Base rates for these splits (e.g. output ≈ 10–20% of input; cached ≈ 30–50% of input in 2025; reasoning tokens growing) let partial disclosures be scaled to a common total. Direction: composition ratios bridge inconsistent provider definitions to the target total.
candidates.data_to_find: Published input/output token ratios for major APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google), cached-token shares, reasoning-token multipliers for o-series/Claude thinking/Gemini thinking models in 2025. Need scope and period. Substitute: OpenRouter model-level input/output ratios as a proxy for API mix.
search_hints: input output token ratio LLM API 2025

assumptions.name: Google late-2025 monthly tokens (definition-adjusted)
assumptions.rationale: p142 reports 1,300T/month for October 2025, while p37/p117 report ~160T/month for late 2025. The higher figure likely includes all surfaces (Search AI, Gemini, API) and is more consistent with p131's 43T/day (~1,290T/month). We use a wide range to reflect definitional uncertainty.
assumptions.applies_when: Estimating Google's total token processing in late 2025 across all products and API.
assumptions.falsified_by: A clear Google statement that monthly tokens were ~160T in late 2025, or that 1,300T includes non-LLM tokens.

assumptions.name: OpenAI product (ChatGPT) tokens as multiple of API tokens
assumptions.rationale: OpenAI API averages ~8.6T tokens/day (p19). ChatGPT has ~800M weekly active users (p71) and likely processes more tokens than the API, but no direct disclosure. We assume product tokens are 1–5× API tokens, centered at 2×, based on the relative scale of consumer vs developer usage.
assumptions.applies_when: Estimating OpenAI total tokens from API-only disclosure.
assumptions.falsified_by: A disclosure showing ChatGPT token volume is less than API or more than 5× API.

assumptions.name: Microsoft non-OpenAI Azure tokens as share of total Azure tokens
assumptions.rationale: Microsoft Azure processes tokens for OpenAI and other models. p156 suggests OpenAI may be 85% of Microsoft's total, but that is an assumption. We use a wide range 10–50% for non-OpenAI share, centered at 30%, to avoid double-counting OpenAI tokens already counted separately.
assumptions.applies_when: Combining Microsoft Azure token disclosures with OpenAI estimates.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that OpenAI represents a very different share of Azure tokens.

assumptions.name: Other providers' 2025 token volume as multiple of Google's
assumptions.rationale: Beyond Google, OpenAI, Microsoft, and Chinese providers, there are many other LLM providers (Anthropic, Meta, xAI, Mistral, Cohere, etc.). Their combined volume is uncertain. We assume it is 20–150% of Google's volume, centered at 50%, based on the fragmented market.
assumptions.applies_when: Estimating the long tail of providers not individually covered.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that other providers collectively process more than 1.5× Google's tokens or less than 20%.

assumptions.name: Chinese providers' 2025 token volume as multiple of Google's
assumptions.rationale: ByteDance alone reported 16.4T tokens/day in May 2025 (p150), which is ~500T/month, comparable to Google's May 2025 figure. Other Chinese providers add more. We assume Chinese providers collectively process 30–200% of Google's volume, centered at 80%.
assumptions.applies_when: Estimating Chinese providers' contribution to global total.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that Chinese providers' combined tokens are outside this range relative to Google.

assumptions.name: Global token volume growth factor from Q1 2026 to 2025 average
assumptions.rationale: p41 estimates Q1 2026 total industry consumption at 30–50T tokens/day. Token volumes grew ~10×/year (p93), so 2025 average daily volume is likely 30–80% of Q1 2026 level. We use 0.5 as central, with range 0.3–0.8.
assumptions.applies_when: Converting a Q1 2026 daily rate to a 2025 annual total.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that growth was much faster or slower, or that Q1 2026 estimate is off.

methods.label: m1

params.formula: (a1 * k_months_per_year + p19 * k_days_per_year * (1 + a2) + p23 + p23 * a3 + a1 * k_months_per_year * a4 + a1 * k_months_per_year * a5) * 1

p19.role: OpenAI API daily tokens in October 2025

a2.role: OpenAI product tokens as multiple of API tokens

p23.role: Microsoft Azure AI Foundry tokens in FY2025 (Jul 2024–Jun 2025)

a3.role: Non-OpenAI share of Microsoft Azure tokens

a4.role: Other providers' tokens as multiple of Google's

a5.role: Chinese providers' tokens as multiple of Google's

methods.rationale: Sum of major provider token volumes: Google (a1×12), OpenAI (API p19×365 plus product a2×API), Microsoft (p23 plus non-OpenAI a3×p23), other providers (a4×Google), Chinese providers (a5×Google). Uses p19 and p23 as anchors. Assumptions a1–a5 fill gaps. Shared dependencies: a1 and a4/a5 both scale with Google; a2 and a3 affect OpenAI/Microsoft split. Failure modes: double-counting OpenAI tokens wit

methods.label: m2

p41.role: Estimated total industry token consumption in Q1 2026 (tokens per day)

a6.role: Factor to convert Q1 2026 daily rate to 2025 average daily rate

methods.rationale: Uses third-party estimate of Q1 2026 total industry tokens per day (p41) and scales back to 2025 average using a6, based on ~10×/year growth. This provides an independent cross-check. Shared dependency: p41 is itself an estimate that may rely on similar provider disclosures. Failure mode: if p41 is inaccurate or growth rate differs, result shifts.

kept.name: Google late-2025 monthly tokens (definition-adjusted)
kept.rationale: p142 reports 1,300T/month for October 2025, while p37/p117 report ~160T/month for late 2025. The higher figure likely includes all surfaces (Search AI, Gemini, API) and is more consistent with p131's 43T/day (~1,290T/month). We use a wide range to reflect definitional uncertainty.
kept.applies_when: Estimating Google's total token processing in late 2025 across all products and API.
kept.falsified_by: A clear Google statement that monthly tokens were ~160T in late 2025, or that 1,300T includes non-LLM tokens.

kept.name: OpenAI product (ChatGPT) tokens as multiple of API tokens
kept.rationale: OpenAI API averages ~8.6T tokens/day (p19). ChatGPT has ~800M weekly active users (p71) and likely processes more tokens than the API, but no direct disclosure. We assume product tokens are 1–5× API tokens, centered at 2×, based on the relative scale of consumer vs developer usage.
kept.applies_when: Estimating OpenAI total tokens from API-only disclosure.
kept.falsified_by: A disclosure showing ChatGPT token volume is less than API or more than 5× API.

kept.name: Microsoft non-OpenAI Azure tokens as share of total Azure tokens
kept.rationale: Microsoft Azure processes tokens for OpenAI and other models. p156 suggests OpenAI may be 85% of Microsoft's total, but that is an assumption. We use a wide range 10–50% for non-OpenAI share, centered at 30%, to avoid double-counting OpenAI tokens already counted separately.
kept.applies_when: Combining Microsoft Azure token disclosures with OpenAI estimates.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that OpenAI represents a very different share of Azure tokens.

kept.name: Other providers' 2025 token volume as multiple of Google's
kept.rationale: Beyond Google, OpenAI, Microsoft, and Chinese providers, there are many other LLM providers (Anthropic, Meta, xAI, Mistral, Cohere, etc.). Their combined volume is uncertain. We assume it is 20–150% of Google's volume, centered at 50%, based on the fragmented market.
kept.applies_when: Estimating the long tail of providers not individually covered.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that other providers collectively process more than 1.5× Google's tokens or less than 20%.

kept.name: Chinese providers' 2025 token volume as multiple of Google's
kept.rationale: ByteDance alone reported 16.4T tokens/day in May 2025 (p150), which is ~500T/month, comparable to Google's May 2025 figure. Other Chinese providers add more. We assume Chinese providers collectively process 30–200% of Google's volume, centered at 80%.
kept.applies_when: Estimating Chinese providers' contribution to global total.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that Chinese providers' combined tokens are outside this range relative to Google.

kept.name: Global token volume growth factor from Q1 2026 to 2025 average
kept.rationale: p41 estimates Q1 2026 total industry consumption at 30–50T tokens/day. Token volumes grew ~10×/year (p93), so 2025 average daily volume is likely 30–80% of Q1 2026 level. We use 0.5 as central, with range 0.3–0.8.
kept.applies_when: Converting a Q1 2026 daily rate to a 2025 annual total.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that growth was much faster or slower, or that Q1 2026 estimate is off.

Method m1 sums provider volumes anchored on observed points: OpenAI API at 8,600,000,000,000 tokens per day and Microsoft Foundry at 500,000,000,000,000 tokens, then scales Google and others via assumptions 1,300 (range 160–1,300), 2 (1–5), 0.3 (0.1–0.5), 0.5 (0.2–1.5), and 0.8 (0.3–2). Method m2 scales the observed 40,000,000,000,000 tokens per day back to 2025 using assumption 0.5 (0.3–0.8).

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
